newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures mostly lower as yen firms.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures mostly lower as yen firms.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended mostly lower in thin trade on Monday, reflecting the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, traders said.
The most-active benchmark October contract finished eight yen per gram lower at 1,347 yen. Other prices ranged from nine yen per gram lower to three yen firmer.

Activity was mainly dominated by trade houses' inter-month trade in tandem with the currency market, while private investors were generally sidelined except for scattered bargain-hunting buying, the traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $379.70/380.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $379.20/70 in New York on Friday.
Some traders said spot gold may firm slightly on technical-driven short-covering, but the upside at $381 and $382 could be tough to break through.

In gold futures, a spreading view that the yen will edge up further undermined market sentiment. "If gold futures fall by around 20 yen per gram from the current levels, private investors could sell gold futures," one trader said.
Platinum futures slipped in line with gold.
Buying by Japanese trade houses in arbitrage trade pushed up spot platinum slightly.
Spot platinum rose to $384.00/384.75 per ounce by the Tokyo close after opening at $383.00/393.75.
Silver futures were mixed, ranging from 1.2 yen per 10 grams lower to 1.8 yen up. Benchmark October was 0.8 yen lower at 177.2 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from flat to seven yen per gram lower, with benchmark October ending down two yen at 423 yen.
